task_metadata.research_topic: causal discovery for observational linear non-Gaussian structural equation models
task_metadata.research_question: Design a causal discovery algorithm that more accurately recovers DAG structure from purely observational linear non-Gaussian acyclic data.
notes: The task_description lists ER15, ER50-LowSample, and ER20-Dense scenarios, but only the five config/stub test commands are mirrored in tests as required by the format.
All three configured baselines map to named LiNGAM-family papers.

tests.label: ER10
tests.notes: Synthetic observational LiNGAM recovery benchmark on a small Erdos-Renyi DAG.

tests.label: SF12
tests.notes: LiNGAM recovery benchmark instantiated on a Barabasi-Albert scale-free graph family.

tests.label: ER30
tests.notes: Larger observational LiNGAM setting where pairwise likelihood-ratio methods are directly relevant.

tests.label: ER50
tests.notes: Higher-dimensional observational LiNGAM benchmark; pairwise likelihood-ratio work is especially relevant in low-sample or noisier regimes.

tests.label: SF100
tests.notes: Hidden large-scale scale-free LiNGAM benchmark combining the task model assumptions with a Barabasi-Albert graph prior.

baselines.name: icalingam
baselines.notes: Matches the ICA-based LiNGAM baseline named in the task stub and baseline edit.

baselines.name: directlingam
baselines.notes: Matches the DirectLiNGAM baseline implemented in the edit file.

baselines.name: rcd
baselines.notes: Matches the Repetitive Causal Discovery baseline implemented in the edit file.

papers.title: The max-min hill-climbing Bayesian network structure learning algorithm
papers.bibtex: @article{fd947c2701d64b079723d5d18251d23a, title = "The max-min hill-climbing Bayesian network structure learning algorithm", abstract = "We present a new algorithm for Bayesian network structure learning, called Max-Min Hill-Climbing (MMHC). The algorithm combines ideas from local learning, constraint-based, and search-and-score techniques in a principled and effective way. It first reconstructs the skeleton of a Bayesian network and then performs a Bayesian-scoring greedy hill-climbing search to orient the edges. In our extensive empirical evaluation MMHC outperforms on average and in terms of various metrics several prototypical and state-of-the-art algorithms, namely the PC, Sparse Candidate, Three Phase Dependency Analysis, Optimal Reinsertion, Greedy Equivalence Search, and Greedy Search.", keywords = "Bayesian networks, Graphical models, Structure learning", author = "Ioannis Tsamardinos and Brown, {Laura E.} and Aliferis, {Constantin F.}", year = "2006", month = oct, doi = "10.1007/s10994-006-6889-7", language = "English (US)", volume = "65", pages = "31--78", journal = "Machine Learning", issn = "0885-6125", publisher = "Springer Netherlands", number = "1" }
papers.relevance: Representative non-LiNGAM baseline family cited by the task background as limited to Markov equivalence classes under purely observational Gaussian-style assumptions.

papers.title: Emergence of scaling in random networks
papers.bibtex: @article{dec997a4dcf4425888ab0fade1b78626, title = "Emergence of scaling in random networks", abstract = "Systems as diverse as genetic networks or the World Wide Web are best described as networks with complex topology. A common property of many large networks is that the vertex connectivities follow a scale-free power-law distribution. This feature was found to be a consequence of two generic mechanisms: (i) networks expand continuously by the addition of new vertices, and (ii) new vertices attach preferentially to sites that are already well connected.", author = "Barab{\'a}si, {Albert L{\'a}szl{\'o}} and R{\'e}ka Albert", year = "1999", month = oct, day = "15", doi = "10.1126/science.286.5439.509", language = "English (US)", volume = "286", pages = "509--512", journal = "Science", issn = "0036-8075", publisher = "American Association for the Advancement of Science", number = "5439" }
papers.relevance: Canonical Barabasi-Albert scale-free graph reference matching the task's SF evaluation scenarios.
